headline: President Donald Trump has dismissed the warnings of AI leaders as a hoax and rejected calls to slow AI down.
score_reason: Pool 9 lowered by 1: the posts date from Monday 12 Oct, before the 13 Oct window; the facts match the headline.
importance_line: A president rejecting the slowdown that the chiefs of OpenAI and Anthropic now say they would accept matters first to the public, then to Congress, back this week with AI on its agenda, and then to AI companies, but he names no policy and the planned meeting with AI executives is reported by the House Speaker, not announced by the White House.
summary: ABC News reports that US President Donald Trump wrote in social media posts on Monday 12 Oct that talk of AI destroying humanity is a "HOAX", that a "SICK conspiracy" is working against AI and data centres to China's benefit, and that AI needs no guardrails beyond "a STRONG AND SMART" president, while Vice President JD Vance said it feels "a little bit" like "a Trojan horse" that AI companies are asking to be regulated. The posts came after calls for a slower pace from Sam Altman, chief executive of OpenAI, who said late on Sunday 11 Oct that his company would welcome a slower pace and consistent federal safety rules, and from Dario Amodei, chief executive of Anthropic, who wrote last week that "we must pace the frontier" (our 7 Oct 2026 edition carried Nikkei Asia's report that mentioned his call to slow down); House Speaker Mike Johnson said Trump plans to meet AI executives this week.
notes: Read from fulltext. The ABC page was open. The Speaker's statement about a meeting is as reported by ABC, with no White House confirmation in the text.
